## Statement

Let \(a,b,t\) be real numbers with \(0<a,b<1\) and \(0<t<2\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
Z&=a+b-2ab,& F&=t^2+2b-1,&
E&=(1-2a)t^2+2Z,\\
C&=(t+Z-at^2)^2-FE,&
G&=2(2-t)^2Z-(a+b)^2E,&
L&=(a+b)E-(2-t)^2Z.
\end{aligned}
\]
Assume \(F>0\), \(E>0\), \(t^2\le 2\), and \(L\ge 0\). If \(C\ge 0\), then \(G\ge 0\).

## Proof

Set \(x=2a-1\), \(y=2b-1\), and \(w=t-1\). These are auxiliary centered coordinates, with inverse substitution \(a=(1+x)/2\), \(b=(1+y)/2\), \(t=1+w\). In particular, \(-1<x,y,w<1\).

Here is a rational polynomial identity certificate. The names in its first column index polynomial vectors \(p_j\), symmetric rational matrices \(Q_j\), and the following scalar generators:

| Name \(j\) | Generator \(g_j\) | Dimension of \(Q_j\) |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| C | \(4C\) | 2 |
| one | \(1\) | 28 |
| xbox | \(1-x^2\) | 16 |
| ybox | \(1-y^2\) | 16 |
| wbox | \(1-w^2\) | 14 |
| F | \(F\) | 14 |
| E | \(E\) | 6 |
| tbound | \(2-t^2\) | 14 |
| pair | \(L\) | 6 |

The vectors and every rational matrix entry are specified in the exact-arithmetic code below. For each name, basis[name] is the vector \(p_j\); upper[name][i][k] is the entry \((Q_j)_{i,i+k}\), with indices starting at zero. The lower triangle is its transpose. Integer digit separators in the code have their usual exact integer meaning. The certificate identity is
\[
4G=\sum_j g_j\,p_j^{\mathsf T}Q_jp_j.
\]
All nine matrices are positive definite. More precisely, their rational decompositions \(Q_j=B_jD_jB_j^{\mathsf T}\), where \(B_j\) is unit lower triangular and \(D_j\) is diagonal, have every diagonal pivot greater than \(1/2000\). The following integers are the exact values of \(\lfloor 10^6\min_i(D_j)_{ii}\rfloor\):

| Name | Exact integer |
| --- | ---: |
| C | 134190 |
| one | 1051 |
| xbox | 2138 |
| ybox | 1026 |
| wbox | 957 |
| F | 909 |
| E | 884 |
| tbound | 1077 |
| pair | 1498 |

For completeness, the code provides the full coefficient data and a direct verification algorithm for both assertions. Polynomials are finite dictionaries of exponent triples with rational coefficients. Polynomial addition and multiplication therefore check the displayed identity coefficient by coefficient. The matrix algorithm computes the unit lower triangular factor and diagonal pivots by their defining recurrences, checks each pivot against \(1/2000\), and checks every entry of \(Q_j=B_jD_jB_j^{\mathsf T}\). All arithmetic uses integers and the standard-library Fraction class. Executing this complete block with Python 3.13.12 returned the nine LDL_OK records with the dimensions and exact integers displayed above, followed by IDENTITY_OK, with exit status zero.

The hypotheses make every \(g_j\) nonnegative. Positive definiteness gives \(p_j^{\mathsf T}Q_jp_j\ge 0\). The identity consequently gives \(4G\ge 0\), proving the assertion.

from fractions import Fraction as R

class P(dict):
    @staticmethod
    def cast(q):
        if isinstance(q, P):
            return q
        return P({(0, 0, 0): R(q)}) if q else P()
    def __add__(p, q):
        q = P.cast(q)
        r = P(p)
        for m, c in q.items():
            r[m] = r.get(m, R(0)) + c
            if not r[m]:
                del r[m]
        return r
    __radd__ = __add__
    def __neg__(p):
        return P({m: -c for m, c in p.items()})
    def __sub__(p, q):
        return p + (-P.cast(q))
    def __rsub__(p, q):
        return P.cast(q) + (-p)
    def __mul__(p, q):
        q = P.cast(q)
        r = P()
        for m, c in p.items():
            for n, d in q.items():
                k = tuple(m[i] + n[i] for i in range(3))
                r[k] = r.get(k, R(0)) + c*d
        return P({m: c for m, c in r.items() if c})
    __rmul__ = __mul__
    def __truediv__(p, q):
        return p*(R(1)/q)
    def __pow__(p, n):
        assert isinstance(n, int) and n >= 0
        r = P.cast(1)
        for _ in range(n):
            r = r*p
        return r

expected = {
    "C": (2, 134190), "one": (28, 1051),
    "xbox": (16, 2138), "ybox": (16, 1026),
    "wbox": (14, 957), "F": (14, 909), "E": (6, 884),
    "tbound": (14, 1077), "pair": (6, 1498),
}
total = P()
for name, rows in upper.items():
    v = basis[name]
    n = len(v)
    assert len(rows) == n
    Q = [[R(0) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        assert len(row) == n-i
        for k, q in enumerate(row):
            j = i+k
            Q[i][j] = Q[j][i] = R(q)
    sigma = sum((Q[i][i]*v[i]**2 for i in range(n)), P())
    sigma += sum((2*Q[i][j]*v[i]*v[j]
                  for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n)), P())
    total += generators[name]*sigma

    lower = [[R(0) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
    diagonal = []
    for i in range(n):
        d = Q[i][i]-sum(lower[i][k]**2*diagonal[k]
                       for k in range(i))
        assert d > R(1, 2000)
        diagonal.append(d)
        lower[i][i] = R(1)
        for j in range(i+1, n):
            lower[j][i] = (
                Q[j][i]-sum(lower[j][k]*lower[i][k]*diagonal[k]
                            for k in range(i))
            )/d
    assert all(
        Q[i][j] == sum(lower[i][k]*diagonal[k]*lower[j][k]
                        for k in range(min(i, j)+1))
        for i in range(n) for j in range(n)
    )
    result = (n, int(min(diagonal)*10**6))
    assert result == expected[name]
    print(name, "LDL_OK", *result)
assert total == 4*G
print("IDENTITY_OK")
